title: Low Water Pressure in Shower: How to Fix It
metaDescription: Shower pressure suddenly weak? It's usually mineral buildup, not your plumbing. Here's how to clean or replace the showerhead and check for other causes.
symptom: Water barely trickles or sprays weakly from the shower, especially compared to other faucets in the house.
partsNeeded: Replacement showerhead (if cleaning doesn't fix it)

steps.heading: Confirm it's isolated to the shower
steps.body: Check pressure at another faucet in the house. If everything is weak, the issue is house-wide (main valve, pressure regulator, or a leak) — skip to the last step. If it's just the shower, the showerhead itself is almost always the cause.

steps.heading: Remove the showerhead
steps.body: Unscrew the showerhead from the arm by hand, or with a wrench wrapped in a cloth (to avoid scratching the finish) if it's stuck. Check the small mesh screen inside — this catches the mineral sediment that causes most low-pressure complaints.

steps.heading: Soak it in vinegar
steps.body: Submerge the showerhead (or just the nozzle plate) in a bowl of white vinegar for 30-60 minutes to dissolve mineral deposits clogging the spray holes. For hard-water buildup that's visibly crusty, an overnight soak works better.

steps.heading: Scrub and clear each spray hole
steps.body: After soaking, scrub the nozzle plate with an old toothbrush and use a toothpick or paperclip to poke out any hole that's still clogged.

steps.heading: Reinstall with fresh plumber's tape
steps.body: Wrap the arm's threads with 2-3 turns of plumber's tape before screwing the showerhead back on — this helps it seal without over-tightening, which can crack the fitting.

steps.heading: If it's house-wide, check the main valve and regulator
steps.body: Make sure the main shutoff valve is fully open (not partially closed). If your home has a pressure regulator (a bell-shaped valve near where the main line enters the house), a failing one can drop pressure house-wide — that's a job for a plumber to diagnose.

whenToCallAPro: If cleaning and replacing the showerhead doesn't help, or if pressure is low throughout the whole house, the cause is likely upstream — a partially closed main valve, a failing pressure regulator, or a hidden pipe leak — and needs a plumber to pinpoint.
safetyWarnings: Don't force a stuck showerhead with excessive torque — you can crack the shower arm, which is a bigger repair inside the wall.
